conventions.convention: Input quantities are square-integrable coordinates of one random element on a common probability space, their means equal the input estimates, and independence is not assumed.
Combined first-order standard uncertainty is the standard deviation of Q_lin = f(x̂) + ∇f(x̂)ᵀ(X − x̂). Its covariance formula is exact for this linearization and supplies no interval coverage claim.

Using nonlinear f(X) requires a measurable output, a measurable definition on any exceptional null event, and square integrability when its variance is used. Almost-sure membership in the model domain alone does not ensure measurability.

Type A and Type B classify evaluation methods, separately from random and systematic effects. A measurement batch labels an occasion or configuration and by itself implies no random-effect assumption or stability.

The example uses input order (R1, R2, Y), exact calibration responses 1 and 21, and a uniform eight-point sign model. Its pooled curve is equal-weight response-on-quantity least squares with a free intercept over four nominal points.

load_bearing.statement: When f is differentiable at x̂, define Q_lin = f(x̂) + ∇f(x̂)ᵀ(X − x̂). The first-order combined standard uncertainty is u_c = √Var(Q_lin). Its use as an approximation to uncertainty of the nonlinear output requires an adequate first-order model; it implies no coverage probability or confidence level.

For d ≥ 1, an open U ⊆ ℝᵈ, x̂ ∈ U, f: U → ℝ differentiable at x̂, and a random element X with square-integrable coordinates, E[X_i] = x̂_i and X ∈ U almost surely, put Σ_ij = Cov(X_i,X_j), g = ∇f(x̂), and Q_lin = f(x̂) + gᵀ(X − x̂). Then u_c² = Var(Q_lin) = gᵀΣg = Σ_i g_i²Σ_ii + 2Σ_{i<j}g_i g_jΣ_ij.
